verdicts.reason: A clips the phone at the top edge of the canvas, so the product looks cut off. Its subline is set nearly as large as the headline and the CTA button is tiny. B keeps the whole phone and a clean left-to-right order, but its headline wraps to two lines and the three text lines are jammed into the banner height. The subline still competes with the headline, and the CTA is undersized.

A has a sensible phone, then copy, then CTA flow with margins, though the headline wraps awkwardly, the subline is too big and the CTA text is small. B jams the headline and subline flush against the left canvas edge with no margin. Its phone sits squeezed between the text and the button, and the CTA floats with a large empty gap before it.

A puts the CTA first, at the far left, so it is read before the headline and the reading order is reversed. Its phone is cropped and jammed against the right edge, and the button is tiny. B keeps phone, then copy, then CTA in a logical order with even margins. Its flaws are the cramped two-line headline, a subline almost as large as the headline, and an undersized CTA label.
